Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you’ve probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it.

We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We’re approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical.

We’re a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

We’re looking for a highly technical, systems-minded Senior Product Manager to lead two critical search intelligence teams: Machine Learning & Recall and Query . Search at Constructor is fundamentally an ML challenge, and this role sits at the absolute entry point of our discovery pipeline, right where shopper intent meets candidate retrieval.
In this role, you will bridge the Query team (understanding what a shopper means across intent, entities, and language) with the Machine Learning & Recall team (retrieving the exact right set of candidate products across massive catalogs).

You will define strategy across both domains, balancing state-of-the-art techniques, such as vector search, semantic parsing, dense embeddings, and LLM-assisted query interpretation, with low-latency production execution.

You won’t be measured on shipping features for the sake of it; you’ll be measured on candidate quality, query accuracy, and driving business outcomes like conversion rate, search-attributed revenue, and revenue per visit.

Set a unified roadmap: Define the multi-quarter vision and strategy across both the Machine Learning & Recall and Query teams, ensuring query understanding and candidate generation evolve hand-in-hand.
Drive Query intelligence: Lead the Query team to push boundaries in tokenization, spell correction, entity extraction, intent classification, and LLM-assisted query parsing across multiple languages.
Advance Recall systems: Lead the Machine Learning & Recall team in evolving candidate generation architecture, seamlessly combining traditional keyword search with modern dense embeddings, vector retrieval, and hybrid recall models.
Move core business metrics: Own measurable lift in search-attributed conversion, revenue per visit, and GMV across all retail customer verticals.
Turn research into production wins: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with ML researchers, data scientists, and software engineers to take SOTA models from research to low-latency, cost-effective production systems.
Balance ML performance trade-offs: Make data-backed decisions balancing model complexity, accuracy, inference latency, compute costs, and real-time execution constraints.
Build evaluation frameworks: Establish robust offline and online measurement systems to evaluate retrieval precision and query understanding accuracy against customer revenue outcomes.
Orchestrate pipeline handoffs: Ensure candidate product sets and query context flow cleanly into downstream ranking and search quality models without signal loss.
Solve systemic issues: Lead technical triage when query interpretation or retrieval anomalies occur, building durable, automated fixes rather than one-off patches.
What Success Looks Like

Stood up an integrated evaluation framework connecting query parsing and candidate recall directly to business outcomes.
Optimized inference latency and compute infrastructure to ensure high-capacity ML models run fast and cost-effectively in production.

Ajaia is an AI implementation consultancy and product studio. We help organizations move from AI experimentation to measurable return on investment across four practices: AI Strategy and Advisory, Workforce Training and Enablement, Process Optimization, and Custom AI Development. Our work sits with executives and the people who do the work, and it is judged on whether something changed in production, not on whether a pilot looked good in a deck.

Ajaia is hiring a remote Product Manager to own products in Ajaia's product suite end to end. You will talk to users and customers every week, decide what gets built next and why, and say plainly what does not get built, including when the loudest voice in the room wants it.

You will write specs an engineer can build from without a follow-up meeting, prototype with AI tools when a working demo settles an argument faster than a deck, and stay on the number after launch and act on what it tells you. This is a builder's seat: you will contribute to the code and the design yourself, not only direct them.
You will work with a US-based team and US clients. Most of your users, stakeholders, and engineers sit in New York, so this role is built around daily overlap with US Eastern hours, not asynchronous handoffs.
Compensation: Competitive, benchmarked to senior product roles in your market, plus a performance bonus tied to product outcomes. We will share a specific number for your location early in the process.
How we expect you to work
AI use is a core execution requirement at Ajaia, not optional tooling. You will use AI daily to sort through usage data, draft specs, and build working prototypes yourself, and you are judged on what you keep from that output, not on how much of it you generated. The tools change fast, and staying current on what is worth using is part of the job.
Remote works here when the writing is strong. Decisions, specs, and priority calls get written down where the team can read them, not held in your head until the next call.

Talk to users and customers every week. Not a quarterly survey. Real conversations, real usage, on US time.
Turn messy, sometimes contradictory signal, usage data, support tickets, sales requests, and what people say in interviews, into a ranked call on what gets built next.
Say plainly what does not get built, including a well-funded customer's request, when the evidence does not support it.
Write specs an engineer can build from without a follow-up meeting: the outcome, what is in and out of scope, where a human stays in the loop, and acceptance criteria someone could test.
Prototype the core flow yourself, wireframes, a clickable mock, or a working demo, when that settles the argument faster than a deck would.
Contribute to the code and the design directly: ship a small feature or fix with AI tools, mock the screen yourself, and hand engineers something running instead of something described.
Partner with the design team on what the solution should be and how it holds up for the people using it.
Partner with the delivery team and engineers on how the build runs and the date it ships by.
Present the roadmap and the tradeoffs to the people who fund it, including when a client or a salesperson is unhappy with the call.
Hold a priority decision under real pushback, or change it, and say why either way.
Ship it, then watch the number after launch and act on what it says.

Highly organized across multiple priorities and open questions at once.
Sharp judgment on what to build next, and clear about what not to build.
Strong plain written and spoken English: specs and decisions other people can act on without a follow-up meeting, and customer calls you can run without a translator.
AI fluent: you use AI daily to sort signal, draft specs, and prototype, and you can tell good output from slop.
Comfortable contributing to code and design directly, with AI tools making you faster at both.
Comfortable holding a priority call under pushback, or changing it for stated reasons.
1 or more years in product management, or work that proves the same skill.
Available for at least 7 to 8 hours of daily overlap with US Eastern time (9am to 6pm ET), consistently.
Reliable internet, a quiet place to take customer calls, and your own laptop.
Legally able to work as an independent contractor or through an employer of record in your country.

Prior experience working remotely with a US or UK team.
Experience with a B2B product used by an operational or compliance function.
Comfort reading usage data or a support queue yourself.
Exposure to a regulated industry such as financial services, insurance, healthcare, or legal.
Prior experience in a 0-to-1 or early-stage product role.

We are growing this team while it delivers, on a platform with real history, and some of what we currently believe will turn out to be wrong. The incumbent HR suites are consolidating and buying their way into this space, so the clock is real.
The problem underneath it is genuinely unsolved. Nobody has built software that knows what a person needs to be able to do next week, teaches it in the few minutes they actually have, and observes whether it landed without asking them. Not the language apps, which have the habit but not the stakes. Not the platforms, which have the content but not the attention. Not the HR suites, which have the data but have never made anything a person voluntarily opens.
If that sounds like a problem worth several years, we should talk.
As our Senior Product Manager for the learner experience, you own the surface where learning actually happens, for the person actually doing it. It is the most visible product role in the company, because everything else in our strategy depends on somebody coming back on a Tuesday. Today weekly active learners sits close to one percent. That number is the job.

Own the learner surface end to end. Onboarding, what someone is offered next, how it arrives, and what we learn from what they did.
Move us from a catalogue people browse to a product that pays attention. Personalisation here is a spectrum, not a feature: country and industry, company size, whether they reach us through their own LMS or directly, then company, department, team and finally the individual. A fifteen minute bus ride should be able to become seven minutes of audio and three quick questions, assembled for that person.
Partner with our educational designers on how it reaches one person. They have decades of research behind how our content is built, in activities of two to eight minutes designed for habit formation. What is not yet settled is how those pieces compose into a path for one person, and you would be one of the people settling it.

Your half is the one they cannot do on their own: how it reaches one specific person, on one specific day, on whatever device they have, and what to offer instead when something did not land.
Own the measurement that makes it real. Weekly active learners is the number this role moves. There is a baseline. Setting the target with us, and owning the path to it, is part of the job.
Treat mobile as a first class question rather than a port. Seven minutes attached to a real week is a phone experience far more often than a desk one. Whether that is a native client or something lighter is a genuine open decision with very different costs.
Draw on a single library. Our own studio content, customer created content and content generated on the spot all sit together, and deciding what surfaces to whom is part of your job.
This role is for you if you have
A track record owning either a B2B2C product, where the buyer and the user are different people and the user did not choose you, or a consumer habit-formation product built to create usage rather than meet demand that already existed
Evidence you have shipped personalisation, routing or recommendation work that measurably changed behaviour, and the scar tissue to know how often it does not
Comfort on a platform that carries real history. You will build the new thing while the old thing earns the revenue, and sequencing that is part of the craft rather than an obstacle to it
A habit of deciding. You gather input properly and then take the call, and you can say clearly what you are not doing and why
A habit of working in the open. Drafts early, thinking visible, and you would rather be corrected on Tuesday than right on Friday
A genuine interest in how people learn. You do not need a background in it, you do need to find it interesting, because you will work closely with people who have spent careers on it
Comfort partnering with an embedded engineering manager on the team rather than managing engineers directly
This role is not for you if
You want a clean greenfield. That is a much easier engineering problem and a much worse bet, and it is not what this is
You need the strategy finished before you start. It is being written now and you would be one of the people writing it
You want to run the roadmap process. Product Operations owns that craft, this role owns the outcome
You would rather own a feature area than a number
You expect to set every priority yourself from day one. A leadership-set integration into the current platform is already on the roadmap when you arrive, yours to execute well, not to re-litigate

À propos du rôle
Le mobile est l'un de nos domaines stratégiquement les plus importants - il devient la manière dont les employés accèdent partout aux outils et au support dont ils ont besoin, bien au-delà du bureau.

Pourquoi ce rôle, et pourquoi il est difficile

Alignement stratégique, gestion des parties prenantes & vision app

Suivre et optimiser les métriques de performance macro tout au long du funnel : notoriété, trafic, conversion, rétention et taux de réachat.
Architecture fonctionnelle & orchestration End-to-End

Empathie et volonté de transmettre aux PM plus juniors.

At GWI we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an extraordinary impact. Right now we’re looking for a Product Manager to play a key role in our User Management (Revenue & Enablement) team in London . If that’s you, and making a difference gets you out of bed in the morning, keep reading. It could be the start of something, well, extraordinary.
Sounds great, what will I be doing? 🤔
As our Product Manager you'll own the systems that make GWI's subscription and consumption business run, such as billing, metering, user plans, feature access, product analytics and user messaging. It's the layer everything else sits on. Get it right and GWI can price, package and sell in new ways.
Two big pieces of work sit at the heart of this role. The first is billing for our consumption products, which is an area we're actively developing, and one you'll help shape.

The second is making our internal tools talk to each other properly, so user data flows consistently between them and Salesforce, and everyone across the business is working from the same picture.

Most of your stakeholders are internal - Revenue Operations, Finance, Business Intelligence, Client Success and Engineering - with some direct client contact along the way.

You'll lead one squad of front-end and back-end engineers and a designer, alongside the PM and Engineers in our sister squad, Identity & Access - together you cover the whole of User Management.

s.h: A few things you’ll be responsible for
s.t:
👉 Connecting our internal user management tools with Salesforce and each other, so data flows consistently and user information is mapped the same way everywhere
👉 Billing for our consumption products - metering, API usage, payment flows and user plans
👉 Customer feature flags, access and management - who can see what, and why
👉 Product analytics - event firing, sign-up flow data, usage data - so the business can see what's happening and act on it
👉 Building the roadmap from client feedback, internal stakeholder input and usage analytics, and prioritising the most valuable work
👉 Scoping the work and owning how your squad delivers it
It’s also fun; shaking things up is what working for GWI is all about. You’ll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and working in a high-tempo environment.
What do I need to bring with me? 🧳
You’ll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you’re willing to learn. Here’s what the team will be looking for in you:
👉 You've shipped products at a B2B company
👉 You've built complex roadmaps with cross-functional dependencies, and you can balance multiple priorities without losing the plot
👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn't complete
👉 You're a strong problem solver, negotiator and influencer — you get alignment without needing authority
👉 You explain complex things clearly to very different audiences: execs, engineers, customers
👉 You ask questions and draw knowledge out of your team to find the right engineering and design solutions
👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn't complete, and you're happy taking a big initiative and running with it
👉 Bonus points if you've worked with Salesforce before, or with tools that need to sync data between systems and internal user management systems.
Equally important is attitude. We want people who think big (to make an impact), ask why (to find a better way), and show respect (to everyone, at every level, all the time). Those are our values, and they’re a big part of what we’re looking for in you.

👉 You'll work on how GWI packages its consumption products - commercial problems with real weight behind them
👉 Your squad owns infrastructure the whole company depends on, so the work gets noticed
👉 You'll build relationships across the business, from Finance to Engineering to the Exec team
👉 You'll learn from a senior PM who knows this space, with room to run your own squad your way
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion 🫶
Diversity is fundamental to who we are—as a data company and as a workplace. Our data reflects global realities, and so must our teams. We strive to build a workforce as diverse and inclusive as the insights we deliver.
As a Disability Confident employer, we welcome applications from disabled candidates and are committed to making adjustments throughout the hiring process—whether that's extra time, materials in advance or a different format, breaks, an adjusted interview format, assistive tools, or flexible scheduling. We're happy to discuss whatever would work best for you.
We actively encourage applications from underrepresented and marginalised communities.
At GWI, you'll find a place to contribute meaningfully, grow professionally, and belong fully.

Zusätzliche Wachstumspotenziale bestehen in der Förderung von Substitutionen und dem Einsatz generischer Therapien bei Erstverschreibungen.
Gemeinsam mit dem globalen und lokalen Portfolio Management stellt der Stelleninhaber sicher, dass das Portfolio die Bedürfnisse der Zielgruppe optimal abdeckt und relevante Lücken geschlossen werden. Zusammen mit dem Vertrieb entwickelt er Kundensegmentierungen, Zugangskonzepte sowie zielgruppengerechte Kommunikations- und Marketingmassnahmen.
Die Kundenlandschaft umfasst niedergelassene Psychiater, Privatkliniken, Spitäler und Apotheken. Voraussetzung für den Erfolg ist ein tiefes Verständnis der Patient Journey.

Dabei arbeitet der (Senior) Product Manager eng mit dem Category Field Manager zusammen, der die strategische Weiterentwicklung der Kategorie entlang der gesamten Patient Journey verantwortet.

Als strategischer Counterpart stellt der Product Manager sicher, dass das Portfolio durch gezielte Produkteinführungen und konsequentes Lifecycle-Management optimal auf Markt-, Kunden- und Patientenbedürfnisse ausgerichtet ist und damit nachhaltiges Wachstum ermöglicht.

· Verantwortung für definierte Umsätze, Budgets, Forecasts und relevante Business-KPIs

· Analyse von Markt-, Preis-, Wettbewerbs-, Kunden- und Portfolioentwicklungen sowie Ableitung strategischer und operativer Massnahmen für die Business- und Portfolioentwicklung

· Mitverantwortung für Preisstrategie, Positionierung und Wertversprechen im innovativen Produktegeschäft sowie im Generika-Business

Ongoing Monitoring is building the capabilities Tide needs to detect, prevent and manage financial crime, fraud and risk across the member lifecycle.
Within Ongoing Monitoring, we are creating a new Acquiring Fraud & Risk team as part of the Ongoing Monitoring team. This team will focus on protecting Tide’s growing Merchant Acquiring business by reducing acquiring fraud, chargeback losses and operational risk across card-present and card-not-present payment journeys.
Merchant Acquiring is a fast-growing product within Tide. We are on a mission to provide the simplest and easiest ways for our members to get paid. As we scale Acquiring globally, we need strong monitoring capabilities that protect Tide from avoidable losses while keeping the experience smooth for genuine members.

As Senior Product Manager for Ongoing Monitoring Acquiring Fraud & Risk, you will own the roadmap for Tide’s acquiring transaction risk monitoring capabilities.
Working closely with Engineering, Data Science, Fraud Operations, Risk and Acquiring Product teams, you will build and scale real-time monitoring solutions using rules engines, machine learning models and Agentic AI to reduce fraud losses, improve chargeback outcomes and manage Tide’s acquiring risk exposure across card-present and card-not-present payment journeys.

About Magic Eden and Dicey
Magic Eden reached unicorn status in just 9 months after launch, one of the fastest in history. We built a category-defining NFT marketplace from scratch and proved we know how to move fast. Now we're doing it again. Dicey is our crypto casino and sportsbook platform, targeting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets.
We're a small, fully remote team. We ship fast, we're hands-on with our data, and we're rebuilding how a growth team operates around AI from the ground up.

Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.
This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. It's explicitly AI-native. You'll build workflows, agents, and pipelines to run lifecycle campaigns that would have taken a whole team two years ago. Half the job is identifying the right problem. The other half is running the experiments to find the answer.

Own retention and monetization as a growth loop. Set the targets, find the leverage, and drive the numbers for everything that happens after a player signs up
Own the player segmentation framework. Today it's value and risk. You decide how it evolves, what signals feed it, and how the rest of the company uses it
Build the AI-native growth stack. Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work
Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Size them, spec them, ship them, measure them
Spend real time in our data warehouse and on-chain data finding patterns and turn them into campaigns before anyone else does
Expand the signals we have on players: on-chain activity, status-match programs, social account linking, and whatever else you can think of
Run the campaigns. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting
Partner with engineering and design to ship the product surfaces that make all of this repeatable

Strong intuition for player psychology and incentive design. Experience in gambling, gaming, fintech, or consumer marketplaces helps. Genuine curiosity about why people behave the way they do is required
Deeply analytical. You can go from a vague question to a clean cohort cut yourself, without waiting on a data scientist
AI-native by default. You already use AI to write queries, build analyses, and automate your own work and you want to push that much further
High output with good judgment. You generate a lot of ideas and know which ones are worth testing first
Bias to do it yourself. You're comfortable sending the email, running the query, and writing the spec, not just briefing others
Comfortable with ambiguity. There's no playbook here, you'll be building it
Backgrounds that tend to fit
Growth PM at a data-heavy consumer company
MBB consultant who wants to move into product and own outcomes, not just advise on them
Product Minded Data scientist or analyst who wants to ship, not just report
Why this is interesting

You're defining what a growth PM looks like in an AI-native company, there's no inherited playbook
Personalised retention is where the industry is going and we're building it early
Real ownership: a segmentation framework, a product surface, and a P&L lever, with a direct line to the founding team
